correctness.rationale: The all-entire-weight statement holds for alpha,m>0, |a|=1, b!=0. For 0<m<=1, power subadditivity makes the translate and inverse bounded, so any W entails a bounded entire multiplication operator and Liouville forces a constant. At m=2 exact square completion yields psi=C exp(-alpha a conjugate(b) z), ||W||=|C| exp(alpha|b|^2/2) and inverse. For 1<m<2 positive-ray Mittag-Leffler diagonal asymptotics force |psi(z)| exp(alpha(|az+b|^m-|z|^m)/2)<=B. After rotating b>0, this bounds psi on the right half-plane and gives global growth exp(O(|z|^{m-1})); half-plane Phragmen-Lindelof applies because m-1<1, hence Liouville constant, contradicted by positive-ray translation growth. For m>2, angularly averaging the same log bound gives a negative term -(alpha m^2 b^2/8)R^{m-2}, incompatible with Jensen lower bound k log R+constant for any nonzero entire psi. The Gaussian and m=1 endpoints are kept separate; zero multiplier is always allowed. The proof correctly uses finite sanity checks only as diagnostics, never as infinite proofs.
